definitions.explanation: The geological process by which rock is broken down in place by exposure to weather — temperature changes, water, and chemical reactions — without being carried away.

examples.japanese: {岩|いわ}が{風化作用|ふうかさよう}で{崩|くず}れる。
{風化作用|ふうかさよう}によって{岩石|がんせき}が{砂|すな}になる。
{温度|おんど}{変化|へんか}による{風化作用|ふうかさよう}が{岩|いわ}に{割|わ}れ{目|め}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: Weathering from temperature changes creates cracks in the rock.

notes:
USAGE: {風化作用|ふうかさよう} is weathering — the in-place breakdown of rock — combining {風化|ふうか} (weathering) with {作用|さよう} (action). Note that {風化|ふうか} on its own also means figuratively "to fade from memory."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {風化作用|ふうかさよう}を{受|う}ける: to be subject to weathering
- {物理的|ぶつりてき}{風化作用|ふうかさよう}: physical weathering

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {侵食作用|しんしょくさよう}: erosion — wears rock away and transports it
- {風化|ふうか}: weathering; fading — the base noun, also used figuratively

cross_references.headword: {侵食作用|しんしょくさよう}
